summary: EfficientNet-B5 paired-view Phase 3 run on the COMBINED dataset (17,269 buildings), warm-started from best_model_phase2.pth (Phase 2 ep5, 74.56%). Phase 3 adds 6 new multi-label and single-label visual heads (wall_features, landscape_features, window, entrance, roof_materials, building_category) with a FROZEN backbone (freeze_backbone=True). Data-prep for this run fixed two parser bugs that had silently dropped 38%+ of Phase 3 labels (Format-A vs Format-B multipart mismatch for window/entrance; missing class_mapping entries for roof_materials). 29 epochs completed; accuracy-based early stopping (patience=8) fired after epoch 29 (no improvement from ep21 onward). Best overall accuracy 72.42% at epoch 21 across 13 tasks.

phase2_vs_phase3_comparison.note: Apparent Phase 1/2 accuracy gains vs Phase 2 best (ep5) are NOT caused by better model quality on those tasks. Two confounds explain them: (1) overall accuracy now averages 13 tasks — adding roof_materials (93.9%) and building_category (96.2%) inflates the denominator, pushing a later best-epoch (ep21 vs ep5). (2) 21 epochs of frozen-backbone continued fine-tuning with Phase 3 targets gave the Phase 1/2 heads modest additional settling — particularly on tasks that still had headroom under the Phase 2 warm-start.

delta_at_best_epoch.roof_type_acc: +13.5pp (largest — still had significant headroom at ep5)

phase2_vs_phase3_comparison.overall_accuracy_drop: 74.56% → 72.42% (−2.1pp): adding 6 new Phase 3 tasks with moderate accuracy (41-50% range) pulls the overall average down, despite individual Phase 1/2 task improvements.

learnings: Frozen backbone is stable: Phase 1/2 tasks improved (not degraded) over 29 epochs, consistent with the Phase 3 v5 data2 result (−0.82pp) and confirming the frozen regime works at scale.

Epoch 21 best (vs ep5 for Phase 2) shows that with a frozen backbone and many tasks, convergence is slower but more stable — no early-overfit cliff. The Phase 2 ep5 cliff was caused by an unfrozen backbone + only 2 new tasks; the frozen backbone here gives a smoother, longer learning curve.

Phase 3 visual tasks (window 49.4%, entrance 43.5%, wall_features 41.0%, landscape 45.6%) are solid first-run results on highly multi-label tasks with 14-25 classes. Context-dependent tasks (landscape, wall) have more noise from viewpoint/framing variation than structural tasks (window, entrance). F1 ≈ accuracy on these tasks means the model is calibrated — not just predicting the majority class.

roof_materials 93.9% acc / 48.6% F1 gap: accuracy is dominated by the Shingles-Asphalt majority (62% of buildings); the macro-F1 correctly captures that Metal, Terra Cotta, and Rare Roof Material are underperformed. The parser fix (adding 'Shingles'/'Asphalt Shingles' → 'Shingles-Asphalt' mappings) recovered 3,895 buildings for this task — without the fix it would have been far worse.

building_category 96.2% acc / 71.4% F1: expected — 91.7% Residential is a near-trivial majority. The model mostly predicts Residential. Useful as an auxiliary signal but not independently informative.

The 2-class precision headroom for entrance and window is real: both tasks have multi-part data where format normalization (window: 'Type:'/vs/'Window Type:'; entrance: bare 'Stoop - Low' vs prefixed 'Entrance Type: Stoop - Low') caused 37-38% of buildings to produce zero labels pre-fix. After the fix, the effective training sample grew ~70%, which is why these tasks performed better than the audit's historical 0.44-0.50 F1 ceiling implied.
early stopping patience=8 from ep21 to ep29: the model genuinely converged — no improvement on accuracy for 8 consecutive epochs. Not a sign of a problem.
next_steps: Unfreeze backbone in Phase 3 (backbone_lr_scale=0.05-0.1) to give the Phase 3 heads access to backbone adaptation. The frozen run provides a clean baseline; an unfrozen run should lift the Phase 3 tasks (especially window and entrance) while risking slight Phase 1/2 degradation. Teacher-distillation retention loss would guard against the drift — not yet implemented.

Label smoothing (--label-smoothing 0.1) on the Phase 3 multi-label BCE path: the window/entrance heads likely overfit on per-atomic labels (overconfident; 49% accuracy with 25 classes means some atomics are near-zero recall). Smoothing would regularize. Run as a single-variable test after unfreezing.
Precision fix (MULTILABEL_POS_WEIGHT_CLAMP): already lowered from 10.0 to 3.5 for this run. If recall still dominates precision on wall_features/landscape, try 2.5. Check per-label report first.

Data quality — the remaining 37% Format-A format residual (entrance 645 buildings, window 16): inspect the complex compound strings ('Porch… . Location: Front Façade; Entrance Material:…') that still drop to zero labels. These are lossy multi-record strings with non-standard delimiters; may need a custom pre-parse pass for the ArcGIS neighborhoods specifically.

Post-training threshold calibration: run scripts/phase3_per_label_report.py on the val split to find per-label decision thresholds. The earlier data2 calibration recovered +2-3pp macro-F1; at 17k buildings the signal should be even cleaner.

Sync Phase 3 checkpoint to S3 and redeploy container to surface Phase 3 predictions in the UI (wall_features, window, entrance, etc. will appear as new task cards in inference results once the checkpoint is selected).
Consider adding the Phase 3 combined checkpoint to the medal pool in the UI — it is the first model with complete visual attributes and the only one trained on all 17k buildings.
